title: Two classifications

blocks.heading: Two classifications
blocks.text: Traditional and modern describe broad educational knowledge and institutions, whereas formal, informal and non-formal describe how learning is organised. They are different axes. Traditional knowledge can be taught in a formal course, and contemporary digital skills can be learned informally.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Traditional education
blocks.text: Traditional education is learning rooted in a community’s inherited knowledge, practices and values; this classification differs from formal versus non-formal provision. Learning through demonstration and participation can transmit relevant knowledge. Practices vary and adapt; traditional does not mean unchanged or without reasoning.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Modern education
blocks.text: Modern education is education shaped by contemporary institutions and knowledge, including formal systems; distinguish this broad contrast with traditional education from the separate formal/informal/non-formal classification. It can extend access to scientific and technical knowledge but needs locally usable resources and inclusive provision.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the distinction
blocks.text: Explain the error in saying a structured school lesson about inherited farming knowledge must be non-formal education. The content is traditional knowledge, but its organisation can be formal. Test the knowledge/system contrast separately from organisation within or outside formal schooling.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
